PullRequest.Title: chat input: refactor and responsiveness
PullRequest.Body:

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call paths, repeated clone insertion, geometry reads, two controllers per input, and dynamic-layout/resize reachability are explicit in the changed code. Exact frame cost depends on picker/subtree size and platform, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM subtree clones, temporary DOM nodes, style recalculation, and synchronous geometry reads
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each layout pass expands every picker and then calls _fitsAvailableWidth once per picker until the row fits; every call re-enumerates items, deep-clones the entire lane, inserts the clone into the live document, and reads several bounding rectangles. The work is therefore roughly O(P * (D + P)) for P pickers and D lane descendants, multiplied by resize/layout and observed-mutation frequency, and two lanes are processed per chat input.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated forced style/layout and DOM allocation on the UI thread can cause CPU/GC pressure and dropped frames while resizing the chat/sidebar, and adds avoidable latency to repeated same-width chat layouts.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, the chat input layout path only updated a width observable (which is a no-op for an unchanged value), while the sessions composer used CSS container queries; neither path deep-cloned picker DOM or performed per-picker synchronous geometry measurement from every host layout.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new loop invokes _fitsAvailableWidth for each candidate compact state. That helper calls _measurePreferredLayout, which cloneNode(true)s the lane, appends it to the live parent, measures each item and the clone, then removes it. ChatInputPart.layout and NewChatInput.layout now invoke two such controllers synchronously, while each controller also installs a synchronous ResizeObserver and MutationObserver callback.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: This added file introduces the per-item _fitsAvailableWidth call at RIGHT line 88; that call performs a fresh deep clone and synchronous measurement for every candidate state. The PR also adds direct invocations from both chat input layout methods, whereas the deleted implementation only set a stable-width observable or relied on CSS.
Findings.Title: Coalesce picker measurement instead of cloning per item during layout
Findings.Impact: Dragging a sidebar/window divider, or repeated ChatWidget layouts such as dynamic response item-height updates, can perform many full picker-lane clones and forced layouts per frame even when the width is unchanged, making the composer visibly janky.
Findings.Evidence: The changed loop at line 88 calls _fitsAvailableWidth once for each item. _fitsAvailableWidth calls _measurePreferredLayout at line 119; lines 159-181 deep-clone, attach, and synchronously measure the lane and every item. The same pass also alternates all compact states and invokes toolbar relayout up to three times. Changed callers at chatInputPart.ts:4984-4985 and newChatInput.ts:1506-1507 run both controllers from host layout; chatWidget.ts:3678 calls inputPart.layout, and dynamic item-height handling reaches chatWidget.layout repeatedly at lines 3797-3815. The constructor additionally runs the same work directly in ResizeObserver and MutationObserver callbacks at lines 50 and 53.
Findings.Recommendation: Schedule/coalesce invalidations to one animation-frame pass, skip unchanged width/content, and measure the expanded/compact intrinsic widths in one detached or contained measurement per invalidation so the compact cutoff can be computed without cloning and forcing layout once per picker. Avoid the direct host-layout calls when the ResizeObserver already covers the width change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or relayout the standard workbench chat composer, including dynamic chat layouts while response rows change height
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatWidget.layout synchronously calls ChatInputPart.layout; the changed method immediately runs primary and secondary responsive layout controllers before returning, so all compact-state updates, toolbar relayouts, clone insertion, and geometry reads block the UI layout call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deep-clone each picker lane into a temporary live DOM host and synchronously read client/bounding rectangles, with repeated toolbar relayouts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one clone/attach/measure/remove sequence per visible picker for each of two lane controllers per input layout; repeated for every host layout/resize/mutation event
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior host layout only set the stable width observable, which did not notify on unchanged values; responsive presentation did not clone or attach measurement DOM per picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks ChatInputPart.layout and browser resize-observation delivery on the UI thread

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective picker count across the primary and secondary lanes, DOM descendants in each lane, and the frequency of resize/layout events. Each controller can perform one full-lane clone/measurement per picker candidate, and dynamic item-height updates can repeat this at unchanged width.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized on the renderer UI thread. The direct calls are synchronous; native ResizeObserver callbacks are also synchronous in the browser resize-observation phase, with no rAF coalescing or unchanged-width guard.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No measurement cache or unchanged-width fast path exists. Every direct layout, resize notification, or relevant mutation recomputes from scratch and reconstructs temporary DOM, even when the final compact state and width are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct synchronous call paths and the clone/attach/geometry-read loop are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact milliseconds depend on the number and complexity of installed picker actions and resize/event rate, but continuous divider resizing and dynamic item-height updates are realistic repeated triggers.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity layout regression: repeated synchronous full-lane reconstruction and forced measurement can drop frames and waste CPU/GC.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or relayout the Agents sessions new-chat composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: NewChatWidget/NewChatInSessionWidget layout synchronously calls NewChatInput.layout, which lays out the editor and then synchronously runs both newly added responsive picker controllers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DOM subtree traversal, deep clone insertion, class-driven rerendering, and synchronous geometry measurement for primary and bottom picker lanes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two controller passes per composer layout, each with up to one full clone/measurement per picker until fit
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The sessions composer used CSS container queries and one width-threshold observable rather than JavaScript DOM cloning and geometry reads on layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the new-chat layout call returns and competes with editor resize/render work

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of labeled picker descendants in the bottom container, number of config-toolbar actions, lane DOM size, and resize frequency. The bottom-lane getItems traversal also walks the container repeatedly during each responsive pass.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized UI-thread execution. ResizeObserver and MutationObserver callbacks invoke the same synchronous layout directly; there is no scheduling/coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cold/warm distinction: each invocation performs fresh DOM traversal and intrinsic-width measurement. No preferred-width cache is retained between stable layouts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both changed callers and the synchronous measurement implementation are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical picker count is small, but extension/provider-contributed controls enlarge both the picker count and cloned subtree; device/browser layout cost varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported responsive-layout finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Collapse toolbar actions into overflow and open a picker from the overflow menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Toolbar relayout computes visible actions and overflow proxies; a user click schedules picker creation/opening with setTimeout so opening itself is off the current menu-run stack but remains user-visible UI work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of toolbar actions hidden/restored during a width transition and number of overflow clicks. Hidden action proxy allocation is bounded by the current action set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Toolbar relayout is synchronous and serialized. Picker opening is deferred by one zero-delay timer; MutableDisposable keeps at most one temporary overflow picker alive per chat input.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Overflow proxy actions are rebuilt on relayout rather than cached, but action sets are small and retained temporary picker state is bounded to one instance. Picker data follows existing delegates/services rather than adding a new cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed overflow lifecycle; no high-confidence boundary fan-out or unbounded retention was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific picker delegates may perform their established loading work, but the changed code does not establish a new subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable performance regression: temporary picker ownership is bounded and user-triggered, while the repeated relayout cost is already accounted for in the reported resize-path issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Relayout other responsive ToolBar consumers such as SCM repository and browser navigation toolbars
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A ResizeObserver-triggered toolbar relayout synchronously scans rendered actions, now checking computed display style so CSS-hidden actions do not consume width.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of actions and number moved into/out of overflow during a resize. Current production consumers have bounded toolbar-sized action sets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous renderer work, serialized per toolbar resize notification.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Visibility is recomputed each relayout; there is no cache, but CSS visibility can change independently and the effective collections are small.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the extra style checks; low for material impact outside the reported chat responsive controller path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Computed-style checks can induce style resolution, but repository evidence does not establish sufficiently large action cardinality or event multiplicity for a separate user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding; this remains bounded toolbar work and is not independently proven to cause a concrete regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 33 changed files. One medium-severity synchronous UI/layout regression was reported: the new responsive picker algorithm deep-clones and measures each lane once per picker on synchronous resize/layout paths without coalescing or caching. No new subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network fan-out, no unbounded retention, and no qualifying regression fix were found.
